brief.setting: Surgical ward, with a venepuncture manikin arm
brief.scenario: Mr Colin Tranter, 72, is day 2 after an emergency laparotomy. He has a temperature of 38.8°C, heart rate 118 and blood pressure 104/66. The nurse has asked you to see him. Blood culture bottles, a winged collection set, chlorhexidine-alcohol swabs, gloves, a tourniquet and a sharps bin are provided.
brief.task: Take blood cultures from the manikin arm, talking the examiner through each step, and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Sepsis first, fresh stab, clean skin and bottles, fill properly, right order, send fast.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Delaying antibiotics to get cultures, or touching the vein again after cleaning.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "He may be septic: I'll take cultures now so antibiotics aren't delayed."

grid.label: Sepsis priority and consent
grid.fail: Takes cultures but ignores his sepsis, or delays antibiotics for them.
grid.pass: Confirms identity and allergies, explains and consents; recognises possible sepsis: senior review and, if high risk, antibiotics within 1 hour.
grid.high: Takes cultures first without delaying antibiotics; thinks about the source: anastomotic leak, chest, wound, urine, lines.

grid.label: Site
grid.fail: Samples from the existing cannula or the femoral vein.
grid.pass: Fresh venepuncture of a peripheral vein, not an existing cannula or above a drip; identifies the vein before cleaning.
grid.high: If line infection is suspected, takes cultures from the line and a peripheral vein, peripheral first.

grid.label: Hands and skin (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Doesn't disinfect the skin, or palpates the vein again after cleaning.
grid.pass: Hand hygiene; cleans the skin with 2% chlorhexidine in 70% isopropyl alcohol and lets it dry; clean gloves; doesn't palpate again.
grid.high: Explains skin flora cause false positives and unnecessary antibiotics; contamination target below 3%.

grid.label: Bottles
grid.fail: Inoculates bottles without cleaning the tops.
grid.pass: Checks expiry; removes caps; cleans tops with chlorhexidine-alcohol and lets them dry; marks fill lines; doesn't cover barcodes.
grid.high: Uses the adapter only with a winged set; winged set: aerobic bottle first; needle and syringe: anaerobic first.

grid.label: Volume and number
grid.fail: Takes one set, or underfills the bottles.
grid.pass: Two sets (four bottles) from separate venepunctures, about 10 ml per bottle, 20–30 ml per set; cultures before other tubes.
grid.high: Volume is the biggest factor in yield, about 3% more per ml; three sets over 24 hours if endocarditis is suspected.

grid.label: Label, document, send
grid.fail: Leaves bottles on the ward or puts them in the fridge.
grid.pass: Sharps disposed; site dressed; labels at the bedside; documents date, time, site and indication; sends promptly.
grid.high: On the analyser within 4 hours, never refrigerated; records antibiotics already given on the request.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll take the cultures first; antibiotics can wait until the results are back.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Wipes the skin, then feels for the vein again with a gloved finger.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Pierces the bottle tops without cleaning them.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Puts about 3 ml in each bottle; one set only.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Puts the bottles in the ward fridge for the morning.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mr Tranter, can I check your name and date of birth, and any allergies? I'd like to take some blood to look for infection. Is that all right? [To examiner:] He may be septic, so I'd ask for senior review and, if he's high risk, antibiotics within the hour.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Chooses a vein in the other arm, away from the cannula, and identifies it before cleaning.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Hand hygiene; cleans the skin with 2% chlorhexidine in 70% alcohol; lets it dry; puts on clean gloves.] I won't touch the site again.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Checks expiry, removes the caps, cleans the tops and lets them dry; marks the 10 ml fill lines.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inserts the winged needle and fills each bottle to about 10 ml.] Two sets in total, the second from a separate venepuncture site, and cultures before any other tubes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Disposes of sharps, dresses the site, labels at the bedside.] I'll document date, time, site and indication, and send them straight to the lab.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll take cultures now, but not at the expense of antibiotics within the hour. Could this be a leak, chest, wound or urine? I'll look for the source.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: He has a central line. If I suspected line infection, I'd take one set from the line and one peripherally, peripheral first.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Skin flora are the usual contaminants. False positives mean unnecessary antibiotics; we aim for contamination below 3%.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: With the winged set I fill the aerobic bottle first, because the tubing contains air. With a syringe I'd fill the anaerobic first.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Volume matters most: each extra ml adds about 3% to the yield. If I suspected endocarditis, I'd take three sets over 24 hours.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: They need to be on the analyser within 4 hours, never in the fridge. I'll note on the form that he's had antibiotics if he has.

failures.move: Delaying antibiotics to wait for cultures.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: delay increases the risk of death in high-risk sepsis.

failures.move: Palpating the vein again after cleaning.
failures.consequence: Contaminates the site with skin flora: a false positive and unnecessary treatment.

failures.move: Underfilling bottles or taking one set.
failures.consequence: False negatives, and contaminants can't be told from true bacteraemia.
Higher contamination and a misleading result.

recovery.when: You touched the site after cleaning
recovery.line: I've touched the site, so I'll clean it again and let it dry.
Winged set: aerobic first. Syringe: anaerobic first.

knowledge.fact: Skin and bottle tops: 2% chlorhexidine in 70% isopropyl alcohol, allowed to dry; don't palpate after cleaning.
Winged set: aerobic bottle first; needle and syringe: anaerobic first; adapter caps only with winged sets.
Adults: 20–30 ml per set; 2 sets for most patients; 3 sets over 24 h for endocarditis.
Contamination target below 3%; bottles on the analyser within 4 h, not refrigerated.
High-risk sepsis: IV antibiotics within 1 hour.

recall.think: Sepsis after laparotomy: anastomotic leak until proven otherwise.
do: Two sets, about 10 ml per bottle
recall.finish: Documented, sent promptly, source sought, antibiotics given.

sources.name: UK Health Security Agency. UK Standards for Microbiology Investigations S 12: Sepsis and systemic or disseminated infections
sources.version: Issue 1.1, 24 April 2025 (replaced SMI B 37, withdrawn August 2024)
sources.supports: Volume the most significant factor, about 3% more yield per ml; adults 20–30 ml per set, usually 10 ml per bottle; 2 sets for most patients; 3 sets over 24 h for endocarditis; contamination target below 3%; peripheral venepuncture preferred to catheters; inoculate culture bottles before other tests; collect before antimicrobials where possible without significantly delaying them; load on analyser within 4 h; do not refrigerate; 2 consecutive sets from 2 separate venepuncture sites per 24 h; with a central line, line and separate peripheral site, peripheral first; adapters not recommended without winged sets; if volume insufficient, inoculate the aerobic bottle first; collection following DH guidance (Taking blood cultures, cited as DH 2011)

sources.name: Department of Health. Saving Lives: Taking blood cultures – a summary of best practice
sources.version: revised 2010 (cited in UK SMI S 12 as DH 2011)
sources.supports: Fresh venepuncture, not existing cannulae; line and peripheral cultures with peripheral first for suspected line infection; avoid femoral vein; identify vein before disinfecting; 2% chlorhexidine in 70% isopropyl alcohol for skin and bottle tops, allowed to dry; do not palpate after disinfection; clean gloves; don't cover barcodes; adapter caps only with winged sets; winged set aerobic first, syringe anaerobic first; blood cultures before other tubes; document indication, time and site

sources.name: NICE NG253. Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management
sources.supports: High risk (NEWS2 7 or more with suspected infection): venous blood tests including blood culture (1.8.2); broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour (1.8.3)

partner.opening: Mr Tranter has a temperature of 38.8 and a heart rate of 118. Please take blood cultures from this arm, talking me through it.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about allergies and observations
reveals.finding: No allergies. RR 24, SpO2 94% on air, new confusion since this morning. NEWS2 10 (temperature 1, heart rate 2, systolic BP 1, respiratory rate 2, SpO2 1, new confusion 3).
Peripheral cannula in the left forearm; right internal jugular central line inserted in theatre.
Say: "Blood flashes back into the tubing."

push.question: Why not sample from his cannula?
push.expect: Higher contamination; use a fresh peripheral stab.

push.question: Which bottle first, and why?
push.expect: Winged set: aerobic first (air in tubing); syringe: anaerobic first.

push.question: How much blood?
push.expect: About 10 ml per bottle; 20–30 ml per set; two sets.

curveballs.prompt: The first venepuncture fails and antibiotics are due now.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Give the antibiotics on time; take cultures as soon as possible afterwards and record that antibiotics were given.

curveballs.prompt: The nurse offers the bottles to go in the fridge until the morning run.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No: never refrigerate; they need to reach the analyser within 4 hours.

curveballs.prompt: You can only get 8 ml of blood in total.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Put it in the aerobic bottle rather than splitting it between both.
